answer: A grove bracket takes an identity on a 70-credit bond: it enters with one ember, a referee draws a duel. A sybil's fable of past wins is checked against the bracket log: a false claimed win burns the bond, the loser's ember is snuffed. The k-th fake buys a new duel entry at 40+6(k-1) credits, 1,000 fakes cost 3,037,000 against a 40,000 pool; a referee fixing five duels exposes a rented ring. An honest agent pays 40 once and keeps its ember.
